newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks jumped Thursday to their second record in a row, their sixth so far this month.
The IPC index added 45.58 points, or 1.09 percent, to 4,240.02. In the broader market, 70 stocks rose while 26 fell on heavy volume of 183.33 million shares.
"Yesterday's rally confirmed the market's upside expectations," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage. "We have seen heavy foreign investment with a long-term view."
Wall Street lent support, as the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 135.64 points to 7,711.47, its fifth straight record.
Dealers said low returns on fixed-income instruments made many investors switch to stocks.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds fell 26/32 to yield 6.78 percent, down from 6.84 percent on Wednesday. Mexican overnight bond rates fell about 2 percentage points to 19.35 percent.
Big blue chips like Telmex and Grupo Carso led the charge.
Telmex gained 8 centavos (1 cent) to 19.00 pesos ($2.39), while the telecomms firm's ADRs ended up 1/2 to 48. Holding company Grupo Carso gained 1.00 pesos (13 cents) to 48.80 pesos ($6.13).
Mining company Grupo Mexico L series headed the prominent gainers list, up 3.45 pesos (43 cents) to 25.45 pesos ($3.20) on news Asarco had sold 20 million of the shares in early trade.
